clue.text: It announced arrival of petty officer's letter long ago

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer, and the possessive adds S
thorn was an Old English letter, used for the 'th' sound and long since dropped from the alphabet

explanation.surface: Some old device heralded the coming of a naval officer's mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text read 'T' for 'It'; the page prints 'It'. A post horn was blown by the mail-coach guard to herald the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The mail coach guard blew this brass instrument to signal that the coach was approaching.

clue.text: "Will, when looking well: can't move her, Looking ill —?" (Suckling)

definitions.text: "Will, when looking well: can't move her, Looking ill —?" (Suckling)

parts.words: "Will, when looking well: can't move her, Looking ill —?" (Suckling)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Sir John Suckling's song 'Why so pale and wan, fond lover?': the missing verb means win the day

explanation.surface: A line from a Cavalier poet's song with its final word left for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Suckling's lover is asked: if looking healthy cannot move her, will looking ill succeed? The missing word is the verb for succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to win out or succeed, exactly what the poet doubts looking sickly will do.

clue.text: Processed bean soups served for appearance?

indicators.note: food that is processed has been worked over, so the letters of bean soups are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tinned soups dished up merely for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' looks like food service, but legal writs are served on people to compel their appearance in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Writs ordering a witness to attend court are formally served, and they demand the person's appearance.

clue.text: Shocking time for farmers !

parts.note: sheaves of corn stood together in the field are called shocks, so the season when farmers stack them is a time of shocking

explanation.surface: Something appalling happens to farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: Shocks are bundles of cut corn propped up to dry, made at gathering-in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The gathering of crops is when cut sheaves are stood up in shocks in the field.

clue.text: A nook in the Aldwych — that's for the birds

definitions.meaning: ... Nook was Ben Travers's farce, one of the famous Aldwych Theatre farces in London
a colony where rooks nest together

explanation.surface: A cosy corner in a London district is fit only for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aldwych is a London street and theatre; Rookery Nook was one of the Aldwych farces of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: First, the first word of a Travers farce title staged at that theatre; second, a breeding colony of rooks.

clue.text: Like stationary motorist eatin' gingerbread?

indicators.note: the clue's own word with its final g dropped shows the same treatment for the motorist word

parts.note: a motorist who has stopped and left the car is parking

explanation.surface: A motorist pulled over in a lay-by munches gingerbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like ... eatin'' signals clipping the final G as in casual speech. Parkin is a dark oat and treacle gingerbread from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a Yorkshire and Lancashire ginger cake made with oatmeal and treacle.

clue.text: Affirm a head for mounting intake of cider

indicators.note: the head takes in the drink, so those letters go inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word cider is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A drinker's head rises to the cider he has downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses CIDER to REDIC, which goes inside PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate something is to assert or declare it as true of a subject.

clue.text: Clarified the penalty being overdrawn at the bank

indicators.note: the penalty is being in the red, so it sits inside those letters

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: An explanation of the charge for an overdraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' (as in being 'in the red') puts FINE inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined, like sugar or oil that has been purified, means cleared of impurities.

clue.text: He doesn't believe his letters were filed in error

indicators.note: letters filed in error are put in the wrong order, so filed and in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic complains his correspondence was misfiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges FILED plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is an unbeliever, one who rejects a given religious faith.

clue.text: The loon cooked over a dying fire?

definitions.meaning: the great northern diver, called a loon in North America, has this old regional name
a fowl roasted above the glowing remains of a fire

explanation.surface: A mad person is roasted over the last embers.
explanation.walkthrough: Loon is not a madman here but a diving bird; ember-goose is an old name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The diver bird was traditionally called this; read literally it is a fowl over smouldering coals.

clue.text: Its thane was no bachelor, said Lady Macbeth

definitions.text: Its thane was no bachelor, said Lady Macbeth

parts.words: Its thane was no bachelor, said Lady Macbeth
parts.note: in her sleepwalking scene Lady Macbeth says that the Thane of this Scottish region had a wife, so he was married

explanation.surface: Lady Macbeth gossips about some nobleman's marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth Act 5: 'The Thane of Fife had a wife: where is she now?' Macduff was Thane of this Scottish county.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish region whose thane, Macduff, had a wife, as Lady Macbeth recalls while sleepwalking.

clue.text: A warning of course specified as already given

parts.note: golfers shout fore on the course to warn people ahead
to mention is to name or specify

explanation.surface: A warning about a course is stated as already given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' points to the golf course, where a shout of FORE warns players ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said or named earlier in a text is referred to by this term.

clue.text: Long to shuffle gently round the hospital?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the hospital letter
to shuffle is to mix up, so the letters of gently are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wanting to shuffle slowly round a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffle' turns GENTLY into LENGTY; 'round' puts it around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthy and long both describe something of great extent or duration.

clue.text: Sporting conversions perhaps — by chorus girls?

definitions.meaning: in rugby a conversion is kicked over the bar after a try
dancers in a chorus line kick their legs up

explanation.surface: Converts to sport, perhaps, among the chorus line.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby conversion is a kick at goal after a try; chorus girls are famous for leg kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby conversion attempts soar between the posts; showgirls fling their legs up in the cancan line.

clue.text: Shakespeare has the measure of Samuel's landlady

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Shakespeare takes the measure of some Samuel's landlady.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel is Samuel Pickwick of Dickens's Pickwick Papers, who is sued for breach of promise by his landlady, Mrs Bardell.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Bardell, in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, lets lodgings to Samuel Pickwick and sues him.

clue.text: Whisker-chopper?

parts.note: read as a kitchen whisk, the 'whisker', or as slang for a helicopter, the 'chopper'

explanation.surface: Someone who trims beards.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisker looks like a beard, but means a tool that whisks; the word is also slang for a chopper (helicopter).
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary kitchen whisk is called this, and it is also American slang for a helicopter.

clue.text: It promises a thumping time joining the service

indicators.note: the time word joins on after the service word

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone vows violence while attending church.
explanation.walkthrough: A massage pounds the muscles, hence 'a thumping time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubdown involves kneading and pummelling the body, so it holds out the prospect of being pounded.

clue.text: Use a gas mixer to cool it

indicators.note: a mixer churns things together, so the letters of use a gas are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to run a gas-powered mixer to cool something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixer' rearranges USE A GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage something is to soothe or calm it, easing its intensity.

clue.text: Are there reports of such a wedding ?

definitions.text: Are there reports of such a wedding ?

parts.words: Are there reports of such a wedding
parts.note: reports are bangs of a firearm, and a hasty forced wedding is named after the weapon

explanation.surface: Asking whether such a marriage made the news.
explanation.walkthrough: A forced marriage is called after the gun that the bride's father supposedly brandished; reports are gunshots.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding forced by pregnancy is named after the firearm, whose reports are its bangs.

clue.text: Kerosene galore from this part of W Africa!

indicators.note: the country is taken from within the run of kerosene galore

explanation.surface: Paraffin flows abundantly from a West African land.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country on the western coast of Africa.

clue.text: Use the cane perhaps to make more agreeable

definitions.meaning: cane sugar is used to add sweetness
to make pleasanter or more palatable

explanation.surface: Beat with a cane to bring someone round.
explanation.walkthrough: The cane is not a beating stick but sugar cane.
explanation.definitionFit: First, adding cane sugar; second, figuratively making more pleasant or palatable.

clue.text: Shell that's cracked

parts.note: the hard shell around a nut is broken open, and a cracked person is crazy

explanation.surface: A broken shell.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracked means both broken open and crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is called this, and literally it is a nut's outer shell that is cracked.

clue.text: Misprint in the true sense of the word

definitions.meaning: a typographical error is so called in printing

definitions.text: in the true sense of the word
definitions.meaning: meaning exactly what the words say, not figurative

explanation.surface: A typing error distorts the exact meaning of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers call a typo by this name; it also means strictly, word for word.

clue.text: Therapy for Struwwelpeter at the barber's?

definitions.meaning: electroconvulsive therapy given as a psychiatric treatment
Struwwelpeter, the German children's book character, has a wild shock of hair, so a barber would treat it

explanation.surface: Shaggy Struwwelpeter finally gets a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Struwwelpeter (Shock-headed Peter) is a German children's book boy with huge unkempt hair; a shock is a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: First, electric convulsive psychiatric therapy; second, a barber attending to a bushy mop of hair.

clue.text: Workmen lead way to make bridge …

definitions.meaning: a team of labourers working together
placed before the word way it forms a word for a gangplank or walkway bridge

explanation.surface: Labourers clear a path to build a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Put in front of WAY it forms a word for a gangplank or a ship's bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew of labourers is so called; leading 'way' it makes a passage bridge.

clue.text: … their boss puts bridge, before gold

indicators.note: the bridge word comes before the gold word

parts.note: contract bridge is the standard form of the card game
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: The workmen's foreman puts a bridge ahead of the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Follows the previous clue: 'their' refers to the workmen; bridge now means the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder who employs a gang of workmen to carry out a job is their employer.

clue.text: Note three points made by: the economist

parts.note: a key is a musical note system, the tonic note of a scale
N, E and S are three points of the compass

explanation.surface: An economist jots down three points.
explanation.walkthrough: John Maynard Keynes was the British economist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the famous British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: Reg wrong in Latin translation of the whole

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes inside the other rearranged word
translation turns Latin into something else, so its letters are rearranged
Reg written wrong has its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Reg makes a mess of translating Latin as a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns REG into EGR; 'translation' turns LATIN into INTAL; 'in' puts the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can be a noun meaning a complete whole, as in mathematics the total of parts.
